receipt: Full Replogle K562 essential screen as pseudobulk differential expression: RapidGLM 1.6.0 bulk-de and edger-ql against DESeq2 and edgeR QL, every perturbation of the screen
host: One AMD Threadripper PRO 5965WX workstation (Zen 3). Timed work uses one thread per physical core on CPUs 6-21, with SMT siblings 30-45 idle; one thread uses CPU 6, eight use 6-13, twelve use 6-17. Drivers and untimed checks use CPUs 0-5.

protocol.runner: validation/receipts/v1.6.0/run_accepted.sh (stage replogle_full) under supervise_accepted.py; controllers are tracked beside the receipts
protocol.cpu_policy: Exclusive Slurm allocation; schedutil governor, boost enabled and SMT enabled, unchanged. Each timed command starts after two ten-second quiet samples. More than 5% other CPU activity on selected cores or any sibling invalidates the command. Host load, other-user processes and vLLM CPU use are retained per command. From the resumed bulk stage on 2026-11-03, a user-authorized runtime service cpuset confines vLLM to CPUs 0-5,22-29,46-47; the reservation receipt records its application and restoration. Earlier accepted measurements retain their original guarded host conditions.
protocol.contention: others_cpu: busy time of the timed CPUs not spent by the measured commands, as a share of those CPUs over the wall time; above 0.05 counts as contended and is re-run.

replaces: 1.4.1 receipt of 2026-10-23 (validation/REPLOGLE_PSEUDOBULK_FULL.json at the measured commit)

data.source: Replogle et al. 2022, figshare file 35773219 (CC BY 4.0)
data.pseudobulk: Lane sums of the pilot (scripts/prepare_replogle.py): one sample per perturbation group and lane (gem_group)
data.skip_rule: A perturbation is skipped only where the pilot code fails on it (dataset construction or a tool); none was skipped.

model: For each perturbation, the pilot dataset (pseudobulk_dataset in scripts/replogle_pilot.py): its samples and the 48 non-targeting samples, design ~ lane + perturbed (intercept, lane indicators for the lanes present, perturbed indicator); the perturbed coefficient is tested.

tools.rapidglm: build/rapidglm bulk-de CONFIG (responses counts.mtx, design x.tsv, last coefficient, threads 1)
tools.deseq2: Rscript scripts/reference_replogle_bulk.R (DESeq2 1.48.2, Wald test, no shrinkage)
tools.edger: Rscript scripts/reference_replogle_edger.R (edgeR 4.6.2: filterByExpr, TMM, glmQLFit, glmQLFTest)
tools.driver: scripts/replogle_pilot.py full-prepare, full --tool T, full-compare (this change)
tools.reference_tools_used_as: black boxes through their public R interfaces

pilot_check.rule: The 20 pilot perturbations of the full screen against the replogle stage of this run (pilot driver, each job alone on CPU 6): tables byte-identical; JSON run records equal after dropping version, paths, timings and fingerprints of configuration files.

against_1_4_1.note: Per-perturbation numerical and discovery changes are recorded above. The count paths have new special-function kernels (VMATH.json), and bulk-de has the separately documented leverage-one Cook rule (COOKS_LEVERAGE.json). Reference tools use the same public inputs.

compression.rule: gzip -6 of every .tsv and .mtx over 64 KiB in the dataset folders
